title: Effective fppf descent for separated locally quasi-finite schemes
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site], with all schemes and families in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. All fibre products below are fibre products of schemes [def-pc-fibre-product]. A scheme descent datum on this covering consists of $T_i$-schemes $X_i$ and isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}:X_i\times_TT_j\xrightarrow{\sim}T_i\times_TX_j$ over $T_i\times_TT_j$, whose pullbacks to triple overlaps satisfy $\phi_{ik}=\phi_{jk}\circ\phi_{ij}$. It is effective if there is a $T$-scheme $X$ with isomorphisms $X\times_TT_i\simeq X_i$ inducing the given $\phi_{ij}$; this is the covering-family form of [def-pd-descent-datum]. Let $(X_i,\phi_{ij})$ be such a descent datum. If each structure morphism $X_i\to T_i$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], then the descent datum is effective. Neither quasi-compactness nor local finite presentation of $X_i\to T_i$ is assumed.

proof.text: Let P(f) mean IsSeparated f together with Mathlib LocallyQuasiFinite f and LocallyOfFiniteType f. The proved Scheme.Hom.isLocallyQuasiFinite_iff identifies the last two conditions with the Stacks predicate [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Mathlib supplies invariance under isomorphism, base-change stability and Zariski target locality for each conjunct. For finite coproducts [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], each component square is Cartesian: disjointness of the coprojections shows that the preimage of the target component is precisely the matching source component. The private proved helper property_sigmaMap then applies target locality on sigmaOpenCover. For the empty family this cover has no components and the locality hypothesis is vacuous.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fppf-family-affine-effectivity-reduction] to P from step 1. Fix affine A and B, a flat surjective locally finitely presented quasi-compact quasi-separated map p:A→B, and a singleton datum on V→A with P. The comparison from step 1 gives separatedness and Stacks local quasi-finiteness. Mathlib Scheme.Hom.singleton_mem_fpqcPrecoverage gives the singleton fpqc hypothesis directly from flatness, surjectivity and quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]; finite affine refinement is unnecessary for this check.

source.place: Tag 02W8, lemma-separated-locally-quasi-finite-morphisms-fppf-descend, first paragraph, reduction to a flat surjective finite-presentation affine cover

proof.text: For the affine datum $(V,\phi)$ of step 2, apply [lem-trf-affine-descent-saturation-quasi-affine-cover]. With $r_C$ and $W_C$ as in that statement, the $W_C$ form an open covering of $V$, and every $W_C\to A$ is quasi-affine.

For each affine $C\subset V$, the $W_C$ from step 3 is open. Apply [lem-trf-descent-saturation-invariant-open] to this same $p,V,\phi,C$. It supplies the restricted descent datum on $W_C$ and says that its inclusion into $V$ intertwines transport for every test scheme.

Apply [lem-trf-quasi-affine-fpqc-effective-descent] to the fpqc singleton $p$ of step 2 and to each restricted datum on $W_C$ from step 4. Step 3 supplies its quasi-affine hypothesis, so all these restricted data are effective. Now [lem-pd-effective-invariant-open-cover] applies: the $W_C$ are an open covering, their inclusions intertwine transport by step 4, and their data are effective. It makes the datum on $V$ effective. This proves the affine case required in step 2 and hence, by the reduction there, proves the item for the original arbitrary fppf covering family.
